title: Regional price indexing and temp-swap hiring probe
summary: Back-of-envelope budgeting and headcount plan to evaluate a regional price-index and a temporary-swap hiring pool to smooth Q1 demand spikes. Combines per-region token volume forecasts, day-rate pricing experiments, and a rotatable temp contractor pool to avoid long-term FTE commitments while preserving SLA coverage.
primary-objective: Determine whether a lightweight regional price index (price multiplier by region and tier) plus a 12 FTE + 30 temp-swap hiring cushion achieves: (1) <5% margin erosion at +25% peak volume, (2) <3% SLA degradation, (3) runway-neutral across three pricing scenarios.
assumptions: Baseline token mix (Nov 2026 telemetry): NA 55%, EU 26%, APAC 19%
Average token cost-to-serve: $0.00018 per token baseline (mixed GPU, quantized models)
Temp contractor day-rate nominal: $420/day, effective productive days=20/month
Elasticity observed in previous Q gives ~+5% volume per -2% net price cut in hosted API tests
interpretation_notes: Base case uses current price cliffs and a blended avg_price. Q1-spike shows ~25% uplift in token volume; cost of serving grows linearly in this model but margin compression is modest due to higher unit price retained. Regional tilt scenario models APAC willingness-to-pay premium and a small price uplift there to preserve margin.
pricing-experiments: Experiment A: -2% global price across tiers => projected +5% volume (observed in A/B tests) => net revenue change: small positive; margin -0.4 percentage points
Experiment B: Regional index (NA 1.00, EU 0.95, APAC 1.15) with no global cut => volume reweights toward NA/EU unchanged, APAC acceptance drops 6% => net revenue +0.7%

Experiment C: Tiered day-rate credits for temp contractors (credit applied to committed capacity) => reduces effective burst cost by ~8% when used; increases complexity and deferred revenue recognition adjustments needed
headcount_plan: Proposal: maintain 12 FTE flex engineers in serving/runtime (across NA/EU), plus a 30-person rotatable temp pool (contractors engaged via vendor slots) that can be redeployed by region-week. Rationale: temp pool reduces hiring lag and keeps fixed cost base lower than hiring 12 additional FTEs. Temp pool sizing based on 20% of projected peak Q1 additional throughput converted to human ops equivalence.
temp-cost-workback: Temp contractor cost: $420/day * 20 days/month * 30 contractors = ~$252,000/month. Equivalent FTE cost for same throughput (assuming conversion factor 0.8) ~ 6.4 FTEs => $118,400/month. Tradeoff: temp monthly spend is higher but allows zero long-term hiring commitment and faster scale-down.
sensitivity_results: Key sensitivities: (1) If volume elasticity > +7% per -2% price, revenue neutrality breaks at -2% global cut. (2) If temp productive days drop to 14/month due to onboarding overhead, effective per-day cost rises 43% and burst marginal cost exceeds FTE equivalence. (3) Regional premium in APAC is robust up to +20% uplift before demand drop >10%.
recommended_triggers: Trigger 1: Hold global price if telemetry shows >10% week-over-week north-america token growth; instead apply regional micro-surcharge to APAC to capture willingness-to-pay
Trigger 2: Stand up temp-swap pool when projected 2-week rolling runway for FTE utilization exceeds 85% for 10 consecutive days
Trigger 3: Convert temp roles to perm FTE only if usage >10,000 contractor-days over 6 months and retention backfill cost > $150k per hire
risks_and_mitigations: Operational risk: cross-region staffing logistics. Mitigation: vendor SLAs, regional leads to manage rotations
Financial risk: temp day-rate inflation during market tightness. Mitigation: tiered vendor contracts with built-in daylight rate caps
Product risk: SLA slippage during rapid swaps. Mitigation: 72-hour handoff checklist, automated runbooks, shadow routing
